key_highlights: ASX closed the week lower as traders positioned for a further RBA rate hike, with commentary urging caution before another increase (#35, #75)
Australian banks forecast the largest house price falls on record; CBA reports home loan applications down 15% since the budget (#64, #66)
Iron ore sector faces a structural shakeout masked by geopolitical conflict, pressuring BHP, RIO, FMG (#37)
Bathla's collapse signals broader construction-sector fragility; ASIC reviews whistleblower complaints at Big Four accountants (#31, #38, #39)
Small-cap miners (Kaoko, Vanadium Resources, Piche, Aurum, Brightstar, Solstice, Power Minerals) led ASX runners, reflecting speculative rotation (#25, #26, #27)
TMK Energy gas rates surge ahead of Mongolian drilling; Beetaloo gas cartel scrutiny intensifies (#68, #73)
EV sales overtook petrol cars in Australia for the first time, driven by soaring fuel costs (#28)
Ratings agencies flagged Victoria's soaring debt; Melbourne councils admit infrastructure cannot cope with planned population growth (#32, #74)

sectors.trend: Iron ore faces a structural shakeout obscured by war-driven demand; small-cap explorers (Kaoko, Vanadium, Piche, Aurum, Brightstar, Solstice, Power Minerals) outperformed on speculative flows
sectors.implications: Large-cap miners (BHP.AX, RIO.AX, FMG.AX) face margin pressure from a potential supply-demand rebalancing; small-cap gold and critical-mines names offer tactical upside but carry elevated volatility

sectors.trend: CBA flags 15% drop in home loan applications post-budget; banks project record house price declines; fee-pricing scrutiny on CBA and Westpac via legal loophole
sectors.implications: NIM compression and credit-loss provisions likely to pressure CBA.AX, WBC.AX, NAB.AX, ANZ.AX earnings; fee litigation risk adds overhang

sectors.trend: TMK Energy gas rates surge on Mongolian drilling catalyst; Beetaloo gas cartel scrutiny; energy transition costs mounting
sectors.implications: TMK.AX and gas-exposed names (WDS.AX, GWO.AX) benefit from rate spikes; transition-cost headlines weigh on renewable developers

sectors.trend: Bathla collapse exposes systemic fragility; housing construction to follow falling prices; Melbourne councils admit infrastructure shortfall; Victoria debt flagged by ratings agencies
sectors.implications: Construction names (WTC.AX, CGC.AX) and property REITs (GPW.AX, DGL.AX) face demand destruction; sovereign/credit risk in Victorian-linked exposures

sectors.trend: Ozempic maker (Novo Nordisk) in trouble, shifting demand toward tablet GLP-1s; EV adoption accelerates in Australia
sectors.implications: CSL.AX and SSW.AX relatively insulated; EV transition benefits battery and charging-infrastructure plays; WES.AX, WTW.AX face fuel-cost-driven consumer shift

sectors.trend: US AI narrative strong (Nvidia, Broadcom, Oracle, C3.ai); Peter Thiel fund in power stock; CrowdStrike upends tech bear thesis
sectors.implications: Limited direct ASX exposure but supports sentiment for CSL.AX (AI diagnostics), WES.AX (cloud), and small-cap AI-adjacent names

Iron ore structural shakeout vs. small-cap mining speculation
Construction sector fragility and ASIC regulatory scrutiny
Energy transition cost overhang vs. gas price spikes
AI/tech momentum from US spilling into global risk appetite

risk_assessment.risk_factor: RBA further rate hike amid weakening housing credit
risk_assessment.mitigation: Hedge rate sensitivity via short-duration bonds; reduce leverage in rate-sensitive REITs and construction

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Record house price falls triggering credit losses
risk_assessment.mitigation: Underweight banks with high residential exposure; monitor NIM and provision trends in next earnings

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Iron ore demand shakeout from structural shift
risk_assessment.mitigation: Diversify away from pure iron-ore exposure; favour gold and critical-mines hedges
Avoid high-leverage construction and property developers; favour cash-generative REITs

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Energy transition cost overhang and gas cartel risk
risk_assessment.mitigation: Monitor Beetaloo regulatory outcome; favour gas producers over renewables in near term

risk_assessment.risk_factor: Victoria fiscal deterioration and ratings downgrade risk
risk_assessment.mitigation: Limit exposure to Victorian infrastructure and state-linked credit

opportunities.recommendation: Tactical overweight small-cap gold and critical-mines explorers
opportunities.rationale: Speculative rotation into Kaoko, Vanadium Resources, Piche, Aurum, Brightstar, Solstice, Power Minerals signals risk-on appetite in mining; gold hedges rate uncertainty

opportunities.recommendation: Overweight gas-exposed energy names on TMK rate surge and Beetaloo catalyst
opportunities.rationale: TMK gas rates spiking on Mongolian drilling; Beetaloo cartel scrutiny could reshape gas pricing in favour of producers

opportunities.recommendation: Selective bank exposure via dividend-yielding large caps with low residential leverage
opportunities.rationale: Despite credit headwinds, CBA and NAB offer 7%+ yields; fee litigation is a contained risk

defensive_moves.recommendation: Reduce exposure to construction and property REITs
defensive_moves.rationale: Bathla collapse, 15% drop in loan applications, and record house price forecasts signal demand destruction

defensive_moves.recommendation: Hedge iron-ore concentration risk in large-cap miners
defensive_moves.rationale: Structural shakeout in iron ore could compress BHP/RIO/FMG margins over 6-12 months

defensive_moves.recommendation: Maintain cash or short-duration bonds ahead of potential RBA hike
defensive_moves.rationale: Traders bracing for higher rates; economy limping, reducing urgency for aggressive equity positioning

market_outlook.short_term: ASX likely to remain under pressure as RBA rate-hike expectations and housing credit contraction dominate. Small-cap mining and gas names offer tactical pockets of strength. Expect volatility around any RBA signal.
market_outlook.long_term: Structural iron ore shakeout and housing correction cap upside for ^AXJO over 6-12 months. Gold, critical minerals, and gas offer relative outperformance. AI/tech momentum from US provides a tailwind but limited ASX direct exposure. 'Bull case returns' narrative is premature given credit and construction fragility.
